desc:
The string expr is an infix expression made of single digits 0-9, the binary operators +, -, *, /, ^ and round brackets. Priorities from low to high: + and -, then * and /, then ^ (power). Operators of equal priority are applied left to right, except ^, which is applied right to left (2^3^2 means 2^(3^2)). Brackets override priorities. There are no unary operators and no spaces.

Return the same expression in postfix notation: digits and operators only, no brackets, each operator written right after its two operands. The result is unique.

Examples: 3+4*2 becomes 342*+, (1+2)*3 becomes 12+3*, 8-3-2 becomes 83-2- and 2^3^2 becomes 232^^.
constraints: expr contains only the characters 0-9, + - * / ^ ( ) and is a valid expression as described
Brackets are balanced; they may be redundant, e.g. ((7))
hints: In the output the digits keep their order. Only the operators move: each one has to be delayed until both of its operands have been written.
Use a stack for operators (and brackets). A digit goes straight to the output. Before pushing an operator, pop to the output the operators on the stack that must be applied first.

Pop while the top of the stack is not ( and has higher priority than the new operator, or equal priority when the new operator is left-associative (every operator except ^). A ) pops everything down to its matching (. At the end pop all that is left.
editorial: This is Dijkstra's shunting-yard algorithm. Scan the expression from left to right. A digit is appended to the output immediately, because operands never change their relative order. An opening bracket is pushed. A closing bracket pops operators to the output until the matching opening bracket, which is discarded.

For an operator c, first pop to the output every operator top on the stack (stopping at a bracket) that has to be applied before c: prec(top) > prec(c), or prec(top) == prec(c) and c is left-associative. For ^ equal priorities are not popped, which makes 2^3^2 group to the right. Then push c. After the last character pop all remaining operators.
Every character is pushed and popped at most once, giving O(n) time and O(n) space for the stack.
